body: Infinite Undiscovery is tri-Ace and Microsoft Game Studios Japan's Xbox 360 action role-playing game, first released in North America on 2 September 2008. Capell joins the Liberation Force in a journey to sever the chains that bind the moon, becoming part of a struggle larger than the life he previously knew. The party moves through the world and fights in real time, keeping decisions close to the action. Situations can continue developing even while a menu is open, giving preparation and immediate awareness a different relationship from a role-playing game that pauses whenever an item is selected.

The player controls Capell while other party members act alongside him. Connect actions allow access to a companion's skills, making the group useful beyond the abilities of the single character directly controlled. Some encounters involve several teams drawn from the larger cast, widening the scale of the situation. The player has to recognise which companion can answer a particular need while the battle continues around them. The system makes cooperation an active part of control: another character is not merely present, but provides something Capell can deliberately bring into the encounter.

Square Enix published the game during a period when Microsoft was supporting several Japanese role-playing releases for its console. Hajime Kojima produced it, with Motoi Sakuraba composing the score and writers including Ryo Mizuno and Shoji Gatoh contributing to the story. International releases arrived within days of one another in September 2008. Reviews ranged from mixed to positive. The game's distinctive interest is the attempt to make a party adventure feel continuously active, allowing changing circumstances and other characters' abilities to remain present while the player decides what to do next.
